In Al-Adsani v. United Kingdom (2001), the Grand Chamber held by a narrow 9–8 majority that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait did not violate Article 6 (right of access to a court). The Court reasoned that immunity pursues a legitimate aim and is proportionate, so it is not in conflict with the right to a fair trial. Among the options, C fits best, though B is a close competing description of the result.

CONFIDENCE: 62
